handshake.proof: device signature over authenticated user/device/connection/purpose/session/incarnation and fresh 32-byte challenge
handshake.authorization: active approved owner device or explicit current member; host output only from the publication's hosting device

checkpoint.payload: AES-GCM encrypted raw deflate stream of the native terminal checkpoint followed by optional bounded JSON terminal metadata (directory, title, program; maximum 16384 bytes); sent only in answer to a participant challenge
checkpoint.delivery: targeted only; a broadcast checkpoint does not exist

raw.payload: AES-GCM encrypted: one marker byte (1 = the deflate stream starts again at this frame, 0 = it continues) followed by a sync-flushed raw deflate segment of length-prefixed byte chunks
raw.stream: one deflate stream for each key generation; the host starts it again at the first output frame after each targeted checkpoint, so a participant always starts at a marker 1 frame
raw.delivery: the host sends output only while a participant is connected or a checkpoint was sent in the last 15 seconds; firstSequence can move forward between frames and never moves back

notice.payload: AES-GCM encrypted: one kind byte, then kind 0 = bounded JSON terminal metadata (directory, title, program), kind 1 = rows:u16be, cols:u16be, atSequence:u64be
notice.resize: kind 1 replaces the snapshot that earlier followed each resize; atSequence must equal the next output sequence of the participant

bootstrap.gapPolicy: resync with a fresh host checkpoint on the same connection, or retryable close; never substitute a plain presentation

freshnessProof.challengeAuthority: requesting endpoint; generated anew for initial connection and every capture refresh
freshnessProof.encoding: UTF-8 text or bytes, each preceded by u32be byte length, following TERMINAL_CHECKPOINT_PROOF_V1 domain
freshnessProof.verification: verify current challenge, exact recipient/publication, host signature and encrypted frame digest before releasing checkpoint or advancing replay state

causes: participant output backlog above its flow control bound
resync.scope: every participant after a host resync; one participant after its own queue overrun
resync.effect: queued terminal frames for the participant are discarded; no terminal frame is delivered until the participant proves a fresh challenge-bound checkpoint
resync.controls: remain admitted for a participant that completed bootstrap on this connection

flowControl.participant: sends received with the nextSequence of the last output frame after each 4096 bytes of output frames
flowControl.relay: measures the acknowledged bytes each second for each participant while output waits; keeps at most half a second of output at that speed unacknowledged (minimum 16384 bytes); holds later output frames in order
flowControl.backlog: when held output for a participant is more than half a second at its speed (minimum 65536 bytes or the size of its last checkpoint, maximum 8388608 bytes or 192 frames), that participant gets resync
flowControl.urgent: controlResult is sent before held output

rekey.trigger: any access change: sharing, leave, friend removal, device added or removed
rekey.host: stays on its connection, stops output at once, makes a new session key and publishes one envelope for each allowed device; one key generation for each change
rekey.participant: stays on its connection, fetches and verifies its new key envelope, restarts its control sequence at 1, then sends resync with a new challenge
rekey.relay: drops host frames, checkpoints, results and controls of the earlier generation without closing the connection

controls.senderProof: AES-GCM under the device channel key; associated data binds sessionId, incarnationId, authorizationRevision, keyGeneration, connectionId, senderUserId, senderDeviceId, sequence and requestId
controls.resultAuthority: AES-GCM under the same device channel key with the control-result label; the relay cannot read or forge it
controls.inputSuccess: hosting PTY accepted the entire input byte sequence; not command execution completion
controls.channelKey: HKDF-SHA256 of the ML-KEM shared secret of the session key envelope for that device (salt sessionId UTF-8, info kodosi-device-channel-v1); only the host and that device have it
controls.staleGeneration: a control of an earlier key generation is dropped, not an error

freshness.revocation: ready=false durably before invalidation; removed users and devices are disconnected at once; all others stay connected and must take the new key before they receive output again
freshness.hostReconnect: fresh key generation before restarting counters
freshness.identityReplacement: never silently trust a replacement pinned identity
freshness.missingPublicationRecovery: same still-live local session; fresh key and connections; owner devices only until friends explicitly selected again
freshness.tokenExpiry: a connection ends when the access token that opened it expires, unless the device proves a newer token with POST /api/me/connections/renew; the runtime does this after each token refresh
freshness.participantReconnect: a participant runtime keeps its open views when the connection is lost, connects again and installs the next proven checkpoint in place

deviceChannel.input: ML-KEM-768 shared secret of the device key envelope

presence.meaning: Backend-reported current participant presence; not an authorization grant or cryptographic identity claim
presence.lifetime: Cleared on host disconnect or access rotation; deduplicated by user for display

termination.boundary: finalSequence must equal the delivered raw continuation; queued output drains before viewer sockets close

connectionRetirement.retiredIds: Fixed-size replay rejection filter; no false negatives, possible fail-closed false positives only for a new connection
connectionRetirement.isolation: Retired controls are discarded without disconnecting unrelated viewers
